weaknesses: The theoretical contribution is not fully convincing. Several decompositions involve unknown quantities such as the true p(z|x) and p(x|z), and the implemented objectives are heuristic approximations rather than faithful optimizations of the stated likelihood objective.

Evaluation validity is limited by exposure/counterfactual issues. The paper assumes unobserved candidate feedback can be treated as zero, but does not sufficiently address bias from missing exposure labels or explain how negative labels are constructed for reranking.

Baseline fairness is not fully established. Many baselines appear not to receive the same retriever-score information, and the score-usage alternatives are mostly simple PRM variants rather than strengthened versions of all competitive baselines.
The online A/B test is promising but under-specified: the baseline, confidence intervals, guardrail metrics, traffic randomization details, and statistical significance are not adequately reported.

Reproducibility is incomplete. The architecture of the learnable posterior, exact hyperparameter choices, training schedules, implementation details for baselines, and code/resources are insufficiently specified.

Some presentation and consistency issues reduce confidence, including typos, inconsistent dataset naming such as Amazon-Books versus Amazon-Toys, confusing DNR-G/DNR-B terminology, and sensitivity plots using NDCG@20 despite the main reranking setup selecting top 6 items.
